stem.text: What action does the instrument on the right plan to perform, and on which structure?

options.text: Blunt dissection of the gallbladder neck to expose the cystic duct and artery

feedback.text: Correct. The dissector is positioned at the gallbladder neck to bluntly open tissue planes, clearing connective tissue to expose the cystic duct and cystic artery — a key step toward achieving the critical view of safety.

options.text: Electrocautery dissection of connective tissue along the cystic duct

feedback.text: Incorrect. Electrocautery dissection is performed by the hook. The dissector works by blunt mechanical separation without applying energy.

options.text: Retract the gallbladder neck laterally and inferiorly

feedback.text: Incorrect. Retraction is the role of the grasper. The dissector is used to separate tissue planes, not to provide sustained traction on the gallbladder.

options.text: Apply clips to secure the cystic duct

feedback.text: Incorrect. Clips are applied by the clip applier. Dissection with the dissector must be completed first before the duct is ready to be clipped.
